ground_truth.description: The test gives the background worker a fixed `await asyncio.sleep(0.5)` window to drain 3 tickets and record the batch call, then asserts outside the finally. Under load / a slow CI runner the worker may not have called `_process_add_tickets_batch` yet, yielding `len(call_args_log) == 0` and a false failure; a condition-based wait (poll until `call_args_log` is non-empty or a deadline) would be deterministic.

Worker cleanup is guarded by `hasattr(ti, '_worker_tasks')`; if the worker-task registry attribute is named differently, `workers` is silently `[]` and the spawned worker task is never cancelled/awaited, leaking a background task across tests and masking the miss. The guard swallows the mismatch rather than failing loudly.

`ticket_store.submit()` is called for the 3 tickets and then the same ids are manually `put_nowait` onto `ti._ticket_queues[project_id]`; if `submit` also enqueues onto that queue, tickets are double-enqueued, which could produce extra batch calls or extra `add_task` invocations that exhaust the 3-item `side_effect`. The test assumes submit does not enqueue, which is not established.

task.title: Batched curator prompt for ticket worker
task.description:
Lift the TaskInterceptor ticket worker (introduced in task 919) from serial (one candidate per curator call) to batched (N candidates per single curator LLM call). Rationale: the add_task site is a known hot-site under orchestrator load; batching amortises LLM cost and reduces the worst-case resolve_ticket wait for back-to-back submitters.

Scope:
- Extend task_curator.curate() (or add a sibling curate_batch()) to accept an ordered list of candidates and return an ordered list of decisions. Prompt must explicitly handle duplicate pairs WITHIN the batch (A is a duplicate of B and both are new).
- Worker: when pulling from the queue, if more tickets are immediately available, drain up to a configurable batch_max (e.g. 5) and pass the batch to the curator in one call. Fall back to size-1 if only one ticket is queued.
- Scale curator budget and turn cap proportional to batch size: config.curator.timeout_seconds and whatever turn cap the curator agent uses in _call_llm must grow with N (e.g. base_timeout + per_item_slack * N, base_turns + per_item_turns * N). Cap the max.
- Preserve per-ticket failure isolation: a failure decoding the batch response for item i must not fail items j≠i. Fall back to size-1 retries for ambiguous items.

Out of scope: worker / ticket design itself (task 919), caller migrations (920/921/922).

Depends on: 919.
